Explore Scarlett → Request a Quote Financial Sponsors The Real Bottleneck in Life Science AI The scarcity isn't algorithms. It's high-quality laboratory data. The diseases that still claim millions of lives each year — cancer, antibiotic resistance, neurodegeneration — are not only waiting on more powerful AI models. They are waiting on the data those models need to learn from. The next great leap in human health will not only come from larger more sophisticated AI models. It will come from laboratories that finally generate experimental data precise enough, structured enough, multimodal enough, and consistent enough for AI to find the patterns that human minds alone cannot. Standardize experiments Reproducible protocols are the foundation. Without them, data from different runs, instruments, or labs cannot be compared — and AI has nothing consistent to learn from. Capture rich metadata Knowing what was measured is not enough. Context — who, when, which plate, which liquid, which conditions — transforms isolated numbers into structured, AI-ready knowledge. Automate execution Human variability is the silent enemy of biological data quality. Automation removes it, enabling the kind of scale and consistency that makes multimodal analysis possible. Verify every measurement Precise, independently verified measurements are not a regulatory nicety — they are what separates data that drives discovery from data that generates doubt. Close the feedback loop When outcomes feed back into experimental design, science accelerates. Every verified data point becomes an input to the next hypothesis — and AI finds connections humans cannot. Aventix Raises €1.2 Million Pre-Seed to Build the Future of Bioanalytics — Aventix Home Scarlett About News Files Contact Get a Quote ☰ All News Funding September 30, 2026 Aventix Raises €1.2 Million Pre-Seed to Build the Future of Bioanalytics Gothenburg, Sweden — September 30, 2026 Aventix AB, a bioanalytics company building sensor-based analytical tools for laboratories, today announced it has raised €1.2 million in pre-seed financing. The company is founded by serial entrepreneurs Erik Gatenholm and Hector Martinez, who previously co-founded CELLINK, later BICO Group. The €1.2 million round was led by Kost Capital and Voima Ventures. GU Ventures invested in Aventix prior to the round. Separately, Vinnova and Västra Götalandsregionen have provided capital support for the development of the technology platform. The funding will support the commercial rollout of Aventix’s first product, Scarlett 01, through its Early Access Program in North America and Europe, the expansion of its applications and software teams, and the development of additional analytical capabilities on the underlying sensor platform. Laboratories generate more experimental data every year, and comparatively little of it is structured or verified well enough to train and validate AI models. One critical area, and the company’s first application, is liquid handling quality. A dispensed volume that is even a few percent off target shifts compound concentration, affects assay reproducibility and influences every conclusion downstream, often without anyone noticing until the experiment fails. Scarlett 01 delivers volume analytics for every well of a microplate without contacting the sample. It uses Aventix Chromatic Core Technology (ACCT), an optical method that turns chromatic aberration — ordinarily a defect — into a ruler made of light. Each wavelength comes to a focal point at a precisely calibrated distance, and the wavelength reflected most strongly encodes the height of the liquid surface. Aventix’s SensVue AI-powered software converts the measured surface geometry into a volume for each well, accounting for meniscus curvature and plate geometry. A full 96-well plate can be measured in as little as 30 seconds. In an independent validation study with VTT MIKES, the National Metrology Institute of Finland, Scarlett measured 10 µL dispensed volumes of DMSO in a 384-well microplate. The reference syringe was gravimetrically calibrated by RISE Research Institutes of Sweden according to ISO 8655 methods at 10.12 µL ± 0.07 µL (95% confidence). Leadership perspectives “We are living in a remarkable time for the scientific community. The pace of scientific discovery is accelerating, but progress will increasingly depend on how effectively we can collect and analyse accurate data to develop, train and apply AI models. Together with a brilliant team, we are approaching some of science’s most difficult problems from a new direction, with the aim of making data collection and analytics faster, smarter and more cost-effective. We are proudly building the technology and company here in Sweden. This financing enables us to take Aventix to the next level and put our technology into the hands of scientists around the world.” — Erik Gatenholm , Co-Founder and CEO, Aventix “Data collection is the real bottleneck in AI-based analytics. We address it by coupling foundational measurements with optical data and images under a layer of AI models and analytics. We started with volume because everything built on top of that measurement inherits its uncertainty. Scarlett makes that invisible error visible, in seconds, without touching the sample.” — Hector Martinez , Co-Founder and CTO, Aventix “Bioanalytics is one of the biggest untapped opportunities to build the measurement infrastructure behind better, healthier products, and Scarlett 01 is only the first proof point of what that platform can become. We’ve followed Aventix since inception, and we couldn’t be more excited to back Erik, Hector and the team as they build it.” — Bodil Siden , General Partner, Kost Capital “What really stood out to us about Aventix is the combination of an exceptional team and a technology platform with potential far beyond its first application. Erik and Hector have a proven ability to build and scale ambitious companies, and we believe Aventix can become a real game-changer in life science tools. We’re excited to be part of the journey.” — Stina Wallmark , Investment Director, Voima Ventures Aventix was founded at GoCo Health Innovation City in Mölndal, adjacent to Gothenburg, and is now based near Sahlgrenska University Hospital in Gothenburg. The company runs an Early Access Program spanning pharmaceutical, chemical, agricultural and cosmetic R&D. In April 2026, Aventix announced a partnership with Eyown Technologies to commercialise Scarlett 01 in Spain and Portugal, followed more recently by a partnership with Wilten Instrumenten covering the Benelux region. Scarlett 01 is available now under the limited Early Access Program. Laboratories can request a quote, a technical briefing or the full validation summary at aventix.io . About Aventix Aventix AB is a bioanalytics company developing sensor-based analytical tools that enable data collection and analysis in laboratories. Its first product, Scarlett, is a non-contact volume analysis system for pharmaceutical, chemical, agricultural and cosmetic R&D, as well as general analytical laboratory applications. By combining novel sensor technologies with purpose-built software and AI models, Aventix is building the measurement infrastructure that trustworthy, AI-ready laboratory data depends on. The company is headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden. Learn more at aventix.io . Scarlett | 01 — Aventix Volume Measurement System Home Scarlett About News Files Contact Get a Quote ☰ Aventix · Volume Measurement System Scarlett | 01 See every µL. The benchtop instrument that catches the errors you can't see — before they ruin your experiment. Request a Quote → How It Works The Problem You ran the assay twice. The data still doesn't make sense. Pipetting errors are the leading source of failed and irreproducible experiments. They're invisible to the naked eye, rarely caught before the damage is done, and they cost labs thousands in wasted reagents, time, and trust. Liquid handling errors directly affect compound concentrations, assay reproducibility, and downstream data quality. Conventional pipette checks are visual and intermittent — errors often go undetected until an experiment fails. Scarlett gives you instant, quantitative confirmation after every dispense, catching deviations before they cost you time, reagents, and results. Here's what independent validation of Scarlett at 10 µL looks like: 10.12 µL Calibrated target volume in independent validation study –0.2% to +2.7% Full error range across all measured wells Validation Summary VS-001 · Independent verification conducted by VTT MIKES, National Metrology Institute of Finland · Syringe calibrated by RISE Research Institutes of Sweden per ISO 8655 3rd-party validated Independent verification at 10 µL volumes Aventix Chromatic Core Technology ACCT How do you achieve contactless volume measurement with sub-micron resolution? The answer is light. 01 Chromatic Dispersion Polychromatic light. Split. Focused. Precise. Polychromatic light is passed through a proprietary multi-lens system. Chromatic aberration — normally an optical flaw — is instead used as a tool. The lens stack intentionally splits white light into discrete wavelengths, each focused at a precisely calibrated distance from the sensor. The result is a continuous rainbow of focal points — a ruler made of light, spanning from the well rim to the liquid surface with sub-micron resolution. 02 Spectral Analysis The reflected wavelength reveals the height. Only the wavelength in focus at the liquid surface reflects back with maximum intensity. The spectrometer analyzes the reflected light and identifies the peak wavelength — and since every wavelength maps to a precise distance, the peak wavelength directly encodes the surface height. 03 AI Volume Computation Height becomes volume. AI handles the physics. Converting liquid height to volume is non-trivial. Scarlett supports two approaches depending on your application. A calibration curve method correlates measured height profiles with known volumes for a given liquid and plate combination, delivering high accuracy where a reference curve exists. A geometric calculation method — which derives volume directly from measured well geometry and liquid height — offers a path for use cases where calibration data is not available. Both approaches leverage Scarlett's AI to compensate for meniscus curvature and surface tension effects. The result is a highly accurate volume figure for every well — delivered in seconds, across every well format Scarlett supports. ACCT is the core technology behind Scarlett — patent pending, built entirely by Aventix. Request a Technical Briefing → SensVue AI Engine Advanced AI. Precise volume. Real results. Scarlett's AI engine doesn't just measure — it understands. Deep learning models analyze meniscus geometry in real time, dynamically compensating for liquid curvature, plate geometry and surface tension to deliver unmatched volume accuracy across all well conditions. Independent Validation · VS-001 Independent validation study conducted with VTT MIKES, the National Metrology Institute of Finland An independent validation study conducted with VTT MIKES — Finland's National Metrology Institute and a participant in the international SI traceability infrastructure — evaluated Scarlett's ability to measure 10 µL dispensed volumes of DMSO in a 384-well microplate. The syringe used was gravimetrically calibrated by RISE Research Institutes of Sweden according to ISO 8655 methods. Calibrated dispensed volume: 10.12 µL ± 0.07 µL (95% confidence). All measured values across three plate rows were within ±5% of the calibrated volume — consistent with acceptance criteria applied in microliter liquid handling verification. ✓ SI-traceable calibration ✓ ISO 8655 methods ✓ 384-well DMSO verification Download Validation Summary → VS-001 · Measured DMSO Volumes Target: 10.12 µL Target 10.12 µL ±5% window ⚠ Well B10: 9.43 µL falls outside ±5% window. Scarlett uses non-contact optical sensing to measure liquid volumes across entire well plates in seconds — no consumables, no calibration liquid required. 01 Understanding based on real data Our AI model has been trained on thousands of liquid/plate combinations to generalize for you your plate and your liquid. 02 Point cloud prediction Our AI model encodes the structure of the point cloud sensor data to infer what points represent the liquid surface in your assay. 03 Flags what humans miss Identify measurement outliers in real time, flagging anomalies before they propagate through your workflow. The Full System SCARLETT | 01 Hardware and software, designed together. Scarlett is built to work seamlessly with SENSVUE — Aventix's purpose-built analysis platform. Together they give you a complete picture of every experiment, from raw volume map to downloadable measurements in CSV, JSON or Excel. 01 Well plate volume heatmap Every well visualized with color-coded volume deviation after each measurement — spot outliers at a glance. 02 Automatic anomaly flagging Configurable thresholds trigger instant flags for wells outside acceptable volume ranges. 03 Automation ready Seamless integration with Scarlett gives you confidence in the performance of your automation cells. 04 Performance data export Scarlett provides the data to allow you to track your instrument performance over time.
